de.meaning: Hanok ist ein Sammelname für traditionelle koreanische Häuser, die je nach Region, Zeit und Bewohnern sehr verschieden aussehen.
de.story: Ihre Räume, Höfe und Materialien zeigen, wie Menschen Klima, Familie und Alltag miteinander verbanden. Es gab also nie nur die eine Hanok-Form.

en.meaning: Hanok is a broad name for traditional Korean houses, whose forms varied by region, period, and the people who lived in them.
en.story: Their rooms, yards, and materials show how people connected climate, family, and daily life. There was never just one hanok design.

ko.meaning: 한옥은 지역과 시대, 사는 사람에 따라 모습이 달랐던 한국의 전통 집을 넓게 이르는 말이에요.
ko.story: 방과 마당, 재료에는 기후와 가족, 일상을 함께 풀어낸 지혜가 담겨 있어 한옥의 모습은 하나로 정해져 있지 않았어요.

de.meaning: Ein Gye war eine freiwillige Gemeinschaft, in der Menschen Geld, Arbeit oder Wissen für ein gemeinsames Ziel bündelten.
de.story: Das Gye in Hangul Sori ist davon inspiriert, aber eine moderne Lerngruppe: Hier geht es um gegenseitige Motivation, nicht um historische Pflichten.

en.meaning: A gye was a voluntary community in which people pooled money, work, or knowledge for a shared purpose.
en.story: Hangul Sori’s Gye is inspired by that tradition but is a modern study group: it is about mutual encouragement, not historical obligations.

ko.meaning: 계는 사람들이 공동의 목적을 위해 돈이나 노동, 지식 등을 자발적으로 모으던 공동체였어요.
ko.story: 한글소리의 Gye는 여기에서 영감을 받은 현대적인 학습 모임으로, 옛 의무가 아니라 서로의 공부를 응원하는 공간이에요.

de.meaning: Sarangbang nennt man das Arbeits-, Studien- und Empfangszimmer im Männerbereich mancher größerer Häuser der Joseon-Zeit.
de.story: Hier wurden Gäste empfangen, gelesen und geschrieben; Schreibtisch, Bücher und Schreibzeug zeigten zugleich Bildung und persönlichen Geschmack.

en.meaning: A sarangbang was a work, study, and reception room in the men’s quarters of some larger homes in the Joseon period.
en.story: Guests were welcomed, books read, and letters written here; desks, books, and writing tools also expressed learning and personal taste.

ko.meaning: 사랑방은 조선시대 일부 큰 집의 남성 공간에 마련된 공부방이자 일터, 손님맞이 방이었어요.
ko.story: 책을 읽고 글을 쓰며 손님을 맞았고, 책상과 책, 문방구에는 학문과 주인의 취향도 드러났어요.

de.meaning: Sarangchae heißt das Nebengebäude eines größeren Hanok, in dem der Hausherr wohnte, arbeitete und Gäste empfing.
de.story: Der Sarangbang war ein Raum darin. Vom Tor aus lag der Sarangchae vorn, der Anchae der Familie dahinter. Gastfreundschaft zuerst, Privates geschützt.

en.meaning: A sarangchae is the annex of a larger hanok where the master of the house lived, worked, and received guests.
en.story: The sarangbang was one room inside it. Seen from the gate, the sarangchae stood in front and the family's anchae behind. Hospitality first, privacy protected.

ko.meaning: 사랑채는 큰 한옥에서 바깥주인이 지내며 일하고 손님을 맞던 별채예요.
ko.story: 사랑방은 그 안의 한 방이에요. 대문에서 보면 사랑채가 앞, 식구들의 안채가 뒤에 있어 손님맞이는 앞에서, 살림은 안쪽에서 지켰어요.

de.meaning: Madang ist der offene Hof oder Platz zwischen und vor den Gebäuden eines koreanischen Hauses.
de.story: Je nach Haus wurde dort gearbeitet, getrocknet, gespielt oder ein Fest vorbereitet; der Hof verband Räume und Alltag miteinander.

en.meaning: A madang is the open yard or courtyard between and in front of the buildings of a Korean home.
en.story: Depending on the home, people worked, dried food, played, or prepared celebrations there; the yard connected rooms with everyday life.

ko.meaning: 마당은 한국의 집에서 건물 앞이나 건물 사이에 열린 뜰과 같은 공간이에요.
ko.story: 집에 따라 일을 하고 음식을 말리고 놀거나 잔치를 준비했으며, 여러 방과 일상을 이어 주는 자리였어요.

de.meaning: Jongga bezeichnet das Stammhaus einer väterlichen Familienlinie, das traditionell in der Hauptlinie weitergegeben wurde.
de.story: Es bewahrte Genealogie und Familienriten und verband Verwandte; diese besondere Rolle darf nicht mit dem Alltag jedes Haushalts gleichgesetzt werden.

en.meaning: Jongga is the head house of a patrilineal family line, traditionally continued through its senior branch.
en.story: It kept genealogy and family rites and connected relatives; this special role should not be treated as the daily life of every household.

ko.meaning: 종가는 한 문중의 맏이 계통으로 이어져 온 큰집을 가리켜요.
ko.story: 가계와 제례를 잇고 친족을 모으는 중심 역할을 했지만, 이런 특별한 생활을 모든 집의 모습으로 볼 수는 없어요.

de.meaning: Dancheong sind farbige Muster, die auf Holzbauten gemalt werden, um Flächen zu schmücken und das Holz zu schützen.
de.story: Besonders Paläste und Tempel tragen aufwendige Dancheong; ein schlichtes Wohn-Hanok war deshalb nicht automatisch bunt bemalt.

en.meaning: Dancheong refers to colored patterns painted on wooden buildings to decorate surfaces and help protect the timber.
en.story: Elaborate dancheong is especially associated with palaces and temples, so an ordinary residential hanok was not automatically brightly painted.

ko.meaning: 단청은 목조건물의 표면을 꾸미고 나무를 보호하려고 여러 빛깔과 무늬를 그리는 장식이에요.
ko.story: 화려한 단청은 특히 궁궐과 사찰에서 두드러졌으며, 보통의 살림집 한옥이 모두 알록달록했던 것은 아니에요.

de.meaning: Bojagi ist ein Tuch, mit dem Dinge eingewickelt, getragen, aufbewahrt oder abgedeckt werden.
de.story: Ein Jogakbo setzte selbst kleinste Stoffreste neu zusammen: Aus sparsamem Alltagshandwerk entstanden immer wieder überraschende Farbflächen.

en.meaning: Bojagi is a cloth used to wrap, carry, store, or cover things.
en.story: A jogakbo joined even tiny fabric scraps for a new use: practical thrift repeatedly produced striking fields of color.

ko.meaning: 보자기는 물건을 싸서 옮기거나 보관하고 덮는 데 쓰는 천이에요.
ko.story: 조각보는 작은 자투리 천도 다시 이어 썼고, 알뜰한 생활의 손길이 뜻밖의 아름다운 색면을 만들어 냈어요.

de.meaning: Jangdokdae ist der Platz am Haus, an dem Tongefäße mit Sojasauce, Sojabohnenpaste und anderen fermentierten Vorräten standen.
de.story: Der Geschmack unterschied sich von Haus zu Haus; Wissen und Handgriffe wurden oft von Müttern und Schwiegermüttern weitergegeben und Teil der Familientradition.

en.meaning: A jangdokdae is the area by a home where earthenware jars held soy sauce, soybean paste, and other fermented foods.
en.story: Flavors differed from household to household; knowledge and skills were often passed on by mothers and mothers-in-law as part of family tradition.

ko.meaning: 장독대는 간장과 된장 같은 장과 발효 음식을 담은 옹기들을 집 곁에 두던 자리예요.
ko.story: 장은 집집마다 맛이 달랐고, 어머니와 시어머니 등 여성 가족 구성원을 중심으로 손맛과 집안의 전통이 이어지곤 했어요.

de.meaning: Munbangsau sind Pinsel, Tusche, Papier und Reibstein: die „vier Freunde des Studierzimmers“.
de.story: Für Gelehrte waren sie tägliche Arbeitsgeräte und zugleich geliebte Sammlerstücke, an denen sich Können und persönlicher Geschmack zeigten.

en.meaning: Munbangsau means brush, ink, paper, and inkstone: the “four friends of the scholar’s room.”
en.story: For scholars they were daily working tools and treasured objects, expressing both practiced skill and personal taste.

ko.meaning: 문방사우는 붓·먹·종이·벼루를 가리키는 말로, ‘선비의 네 친구’라고 불렀어요.
ko.story: 선비에게는 매일 쓰는 사랑방 도구이면서 솜씨와 취향을 드러내는 아끼는 물건이기도 했어요.

de.meaning: Maehwa ist die Pflaumenblüte, die oft schon in der Kälte am Ende des Winters erscheint.
de.story: In der Gelehrtenkultur stand ihr frühes Blühen für Standhaftigkeit und Lauterkeit; deshalb begegnet sie häufig in Bildern und Schreibgeräten.

en.meaning: Maehwa is the plum blossom, which often appears in the cold near winter’s end.
en.story: In scholar culture, its early bloom represented resilience and integrity, so it often appeared in paintings and writing objects.

ko.meaning: 매화는 겨울이 채 끝나기 전 추위 속에서도 피어나는 매실나무의 꽃이에요.
ko.story: 선비 문화에서는 일찍 피는 모습이 절개와 지조를 떠올리게 해 그림과 문방구의 무늬로 자주 만날 수 있어요.

de.meaning: Sagunja, die „vier Edlen“, sind Pflaumenblüte, Orchidee, Chrysantheme und Bambus.
de.story: Ihre Eigenschaften wurden mit Lauterkeit und Haltung verbunden; beim Malen übten Gelehrte deshalb nicht nur Technik, sondern auch ihr Idealbild.

en.meaning: Sagunja, the “four gentlemen,” are the plum blossom, orchid, chrysanthemum, and bamboo.
en.story: Their qualities were linked to integrity and principle, so painting them practiced not only technique but also a scholar’s ideals.

ko.meaning: 사군자는 매화·난초·국화·대나무, 네 식물을 함께 이르는 말이에요.
ko.story: 각 식물의 성질을 절개와 지조에 빗대어, 선비들은 그림 솜씨뿐 아니라 자신이 바라는 마음가짐도 함께 표현했어요.

de.meaning: Gat ist ein Sammelname für traditionelle koreanische Kopfbedeckungen; bekannt ist besonders der schwarze Hut mit breiter Krempe.
de.story: In der Joseon-Zeit gehörte er zur Kleidung erwachsener Männer und konnte Anlass, Rang und gesellschaftliche Regeln sichtbar machen.

en.meaning: Gat is a broad name for traditional Korean headwear; the black hat with a wide brim is the best-known form.
en.story: In the Joseon period it formed part of adult men’s dress and could make occasion, rank, and social rules visible.

ko.meaning: 갓은 한국의 전통 관모를 넓게 이르는 말이며, 그중 검고 챙이 넓은 흑립이 잘 알려져 있어요.
ko.story: 조선시대 성인 남성의 차림에 쓰였고, 때와 신분에 따른 사회의 복식 규범을 눈에 보이게 하기도 했어요.

de.meaning: Chaekgado ist ein Bild von Bücherregalen, in denen Bücher zusammen mit Schreibzeug, Gefäßen, Blumen und Kostbarkeiten stehen.
de.story: Es brachte die Freude an Büchern und den Wunsch nach Bildung sichtbar ins Zimmer; später wurden Motive und Publikum vielfältiger.

en.meaning: Chaekgado is a painting of bookshelves filled with books, writing tools, vessels, flowers, and treasured objects.
en.story: It brought delight in books and aspirations for learning into the room; over time, its motifs and audience became more varied.

ko.meaning: 책가도는 책장 속 책과 문방구, 그릇, 꽃, 귀한 물건들을 함께 그린 그림이에요.
ko.story: 책을 아끼는 마음과 배움에 대한 바람을 방 안에 펼쳐 보였고, 시간이 흐르며 소재와 즐기는 사람도 다양해졌어요.

de.meaning: Soban ist ein kleiner tragbarer Tisch, auf dem Speisen ins Zimmer gebracht und serviert wurden.
de.story: Da Küche und Esszimmer oft getrennt waren, war er besonders praktisch; regionale Formen und Handwerk machten jeden Typ unverwechselbar.

en.meaning: A soban is a small portable table used to carry food into a room and serve it there.
en.story: It was practical when kitchens and dining rooms were apart; regional forms and craftsmanship gave each type a distinct character.

ko.meaning: 소반은 음식을 방으로 나르고 그 위에 차려 먹는 데 쓰던 작고 옮기기 쉬운 상이에요.
ko.story: 부엌과 식사하는 방이 떨어진 집에서 특히 실용적이었고, 지역마다 다른 모양과 장인의 솜씨도 담겼어요.

de.meaning: Ein Jagae-mungap ist ein niedriger Schrank, dessen lackierte Oberfläche mit dünn geschliffenen Muschelschalen verziert ist.
de.story: Je nach Zeit und Besitzer verbanden solche Möbel Aufbewahrung mit schimmernden Mustern; aufwendige Stücke waren besondere, nicht alltägliche Besitztümer.

en.meaning: A jagae mungap is a low cabinet with a lacquered surface decorated using thinly polished pieces of shell.
en.story: Depending on period and owner, such furniture joined storage with shimmering patterns; elaborate pieces were special rather than everyday possessions.

ko.meaning: 자개문갑은 낮은 수납가구의 옻칠한 표면을 얇게 간 조개껍데기 조각으로 꾸민 물건이에요.
ko.story: 시대와 주인에 따라 수납과 반짝이는 무늬를 함께 즐겼으며, 공들인 자개 가구는 누구에게나 흔한 살림은 아니었어요.

de.meaning: Ein Dojangcheop ist ein Album, in dem Abdrücke von Dojang, geschnitzten Namens- und Kunststempeln, gesammelt wurden.
de.story: In Hangul Sori füllt sich dein Dojangcheop mit Dancheong-Stempeln: Jedes abgeschlossene Wortpaket hinterlässt einen Abdruck.

en.meaning: A dojangcheop is an album that collected impressions of dojang, carved personal name and art seals.
en.story: In Hangul Sori, your dojangcheop fills with dancheong stamps: every finished word pack leaves an imprint.

ko.meaning: 도장첩은 이름이나 그림에 쓰는 도장을 찍어 모아 두던 첩이에요.
ko.story: 한글소리에서는 단청 도장으로 도장첩이 채워져요. 단어 꾸러미를 마칠 때마다 도장이 하나씩 찍혀요.

de.meaning: Die Elster (까치) gilt in Korea traditionell als Glücksbote: Ihr Ruf soll gute Nachrichten und Besuch ankündigen.
de.story: In Volksbildern neckt die selbstbewusste Elster den mächtigen Tiger. Ihr Nest im Hanok erinnert an Hangul Soris eigenes Elstern-Maskottchen.

en.meaning: The magpie (까치) is traditionally seen in Korea as a bearer of good luck: its call is said to announce good news and visitors.
en.story: In folk paintings, the confident magpie teases the mighty tiger. Its nest in your hanok echoes Hangul Sori's own magpie mascot.

ko.meaning: 까치는 한국에서 전통적으로 좋은 소식과 손님을 알리는 길조로 여겨졌어요.
ko.story: 까치호랑이 민화에서 까치는 당당하게 호랑이를 놀리듯 그려져요. 한옥에 놓인 둥지는 한글소리의 까치 마스코트와도 이어져요.

sources.title: The Korea Times Tigers and Magpies at Leeum

de.meaning: Daecheong ist die breite, offene Holzdiele in der Mitte eines Hanok, die die Zimmer der Familie miteinander verbindet.
de.story: Bei Hochzeiten, Ahnenriten und großen Festen versammelte sich hier die ganze Familie; im Sommer diente die luftige Diele auch als kühler Rückzugsort.

en.meaning: Daecheong is the broad, open wooden-floored hall at the center of a hanok, connecting the family's rooms to one another.
en.story: Weddings, ancestral rites, and big family events gathered everyone here; in summer the airy floor also served as a cool retreat from the heat.

ko.meaning: 대청은 한옥 가운데에 있는 넓은 나무 마루로, 방과 방을 이어주는 공간이에요.
ko.story: 혼례나 제사 같은 집안의 큰 행사가 이곳에서 열렸고, 바람이 잘 통해 여름에는 시원한 쉼터가 되기도 했어요.

de.meaning: Haengnangchae nennt man die Gebäudereihe beiderseits des Haupttors, in der Bedienstete wohnten und Vorräte lagerten.
de.story: Ställe, Kammern und Lagerräume reihten sich hier aneinander; bei großen Häusern konnte dieser Trakt viele Räume umfassen, bei einfachen Höfen fehlte er oft ganz.

en.meaning: Haengnangchae is the row of rooms on either side of the main gate, where servants lived and household supplies were stored.
en.story: Stables, small rooms, and storage lined up here side by side; a large estate could hold many such rooms, while a modest household often had none at all.

ko.meaning: 행랑채는 대문 양쪽에 늘어선 건물로, 일꾼들이 지내고 살림살이를 두던 곳이에요.
ko.story: 마구간과 방, 곳간이 나란히 있었고, 큰 집은 방이 여러 칸이었지만 작은 살림집에는 아예 없기도 했어요.

de.meaning: Anchae ist der innerste Wohnbereich eines Hanok, in dem die Frauen des Hauses lebten und den Alltag lenkten.
de.story: Ein Zwischengang oder Innentor trennte ihn vom Sarangchae; nur Familie und weibliche Gäste durften diesen geschützten Bereich betreten.

en.meaning: Anchae is the innermost living area of a hanok, where the women of the household lived and ran daily life.
en.story: An inner corridor or middle gate separated it from the sarangchae; only family and female guests were welcomed into this protected space.

ko.meaning: 안채는 한옥의 가장 안쪽에 있는 살림 공간으로, 집안 여성들이 지내며 살림을 이끌던 곳이에요.
ko.story: 사랑채와는 중문이나 복도로 나뉘어 있었고, 가족과 여성 손님만 드나들 수 있는 곳이었어요.

de.meaning: Huwon ist der Garten hinter dem Hauptgebäude eines Hanok, oft in Terrassen an einem Hang angelegt.
de.story: Steinstufen folgten dem natürlichen Gefälle, dazwischen wuchsen Blumen und Bäume; hier fand die Familie einen ruhigen Rückzugsort abseits des Alltags.

en.meaning: Huwon is the garden behind a hanok's main building, often laid out in terraces that follow a hillside.
en.story: Stone steps followed the natural slope, with flowers and trees planted between them; here the family found a quiet retreat away from daily life.

ko.meaning: 후원은 한옥 본채 뒤에 있는 정원으로, 흔히 언덕의 경사를 살려 계단식으로 꾸몄어요.
ko.story: 돌계단 사이사이에 꽃과 나무를 심어, 가족이 일상에서 벗어나 조용히 쉴 수 있는 공간이 되었어요.

de.meaning: Sadang ist das Gebäude, in dem eine Familie die Gedenktafeln ihrer Ahnen aufbewahrte und ihnen Riten widmete.
de.story: Es stand meist im hintersten, ruhigsten Teil des Grundstücks, oft von einer eigenen Mauer umgeben; nicht jeder durfte diesen heiligen Ort einfach betreten.

en.meaning: Sadang is the building where a family kept its ancestors' memorial tablets and performed rites in their honor.
en.story: It usually stood in the deepest, quietest part of the property, often behind its own wall; not everyone was free to simply walk in.

ko.meaning: 사당은 조상의 위패를 모시고 제사를 지내던 건물이에요.
ko.story: 집에서 가장 깊고 조용한 자리에 담장을 두르고 자리했으며, 누구나 함부로 드나들 수 있는 곳은 아니었어요.
